setting_and_object.category: Phenomenon (mechanistic analysis of reasoning in diffusion video models)

details: Diffusion video generators show non-trivial reasoning ability, previously attributed to a 'Chain-of-Frames' (CoF) mechanism unfolding sequentially across frames; the actual mechanism was unexamined.

Chain-of-Steps (CoS): the claim/finding that reasoning in diffusion video models emerges along denoising steps rather than across frames, with early steps holding multiple candidate solutions (multi-path or superposed) that are progressively pruned into one answer.

Method to expose it: decode the per-step estimated clean latent x̂0 = x_s − σ_s·v_θ(x_s,s,c) as an interpretable snapshot of the model's current hypothesis, plus step- vs frame-level noise perturbation to localize where reasoning lives.
Proof-of-concept exploit: Training-Free Ensemble (TFE), averaging mid-layer DiT latents from several same-model runs with different seeds at the first denoising step.
Base video generators: Wan2.1, Wan2.2 (I2V-A14B), LTX2.3.
Reasoning-enhanced variants via LoRA tuned on VBVR (prefixed VBVR-); VBVR-Wan2.2 is the main model used for visualizations.
Additional test: 4-step Phased-DMD distilled Wan2.2-I2V-14B combined with the reasoning LoRA (both at weight 0.5).
VBVR-Bench (with in-domain / out-of-domain splits), V-Reason Bench, MME-CoF, RISE-Video; qualitative examples also from VBench.
Task types: maze/robot navigation, tic-tac-toe, object movement/rotation, shape detection, pattern completion, object permanence.

Noise injection: Gaussian noise replacing all frames at one diffusion step ('Noise at Step') vs one frame across all steps ('Noise at Frame'); CKA dissimilarity used to trace propagation of the perturbation.
Layer-wise token energy maps (channel-wise L2 norm of hidden states, 40 DiT blocks, reshaped to f×h×w grid) from forward hooks at each step.

Layer-wise latent swapping: two forward passes with object configurations O_A/O_B; replace layer-k representation with the alternative and measure grounding flip rate over 10 object-category pairs x 5 seeds.
Manual inspection of 200 examples from VBVR-Bench and real videos to gauge prevalence; 'candidate multiplicity' counted per step.
Default: 3 seeds, spatial-temporal averaging of hidden representations across mid-layers 20-29 at the first diffusion step (s=0).
Ablations: ensemble size 1-6 seeds; aggregation window layers 0-9 vs 0-39 vs 20-29.
Frame-count study: single-frame (ChronoEdit-style RoPE anchoring, image-editing repurposing) vs multi-frame, and reducing ~100 frames down to 17 and below.

key_findings.finding: Reasoning in diffusion video models unfolds along denoising steps (Chain-of-Steps), not sequentially across frames as the Chain-of-Frames hypothesis assumes.
key_findings.evidence: Injecting Gaussian noise into all frames at a single diffusion step collapses the VBVR-Bench score from 0.685 to below 0.3, while noising one frame across all steps causes a far smaller drop; bidirectional attention lets corrupted frames be recovered from neighbors. Decoded x̂0 trajectories show candidate solutions spawned early and pruned over steps.

key_findings.finding: Two structured exploration modes are visible in intermediate step-wise predictions: multi-path exploration (BFS-like branch pruning) and superposition-based exploration (overlapping mutually exclusive states).
key_findings.evidence: Examples include a robot exploring both maze routes before one dominates, multiple candidate tic-tac-toe cells, four object trajectories collapsing to one shelf layer, and superposed circle sizes/rotation angles. 72% of 200 manually inspected examples show one of the two behaviors; candidate multiplicity is markedly higher for reasoning-enhanced VBVR-Wan2.2 than for general generation baselines.

key_findings.finding: Middle diffusion steps and middle DiT layers are the causally decisive locus of reasoning.
key_findings.evidence: CKA dissimilarity after step-wise noise injection peaks in sensitivity around steps 20-30 and early-step perturbations propagate through the whole trajectory; swapping a single layer's latent (roughly layers 15-35) flips the grounding target, with flip-rate curves bell-shaped across 10 category pairs and 5 seeds.

key_findings.finding: Training-Free Ensemble, which averages mid-layer latents across seeds at the first step, consistently improves reasoning without training.
key_findings.evidence: VBVR-Wan2.2 gains 4.3% on VBVR-Bench, 35.6% on V-Reason Bench, 16.9% on MME-CoF, 6.9% on RISE-Video (similar for VBVR-Wan2.1 and VBVR-LTX2.3); ablations show mid-layers 20-29 (0.716) beat layers 0-9 (0.688) and all layers (0.690) against 0.685 baseline, and 3-4 seeds are optimal (0.716-0.729) with degradation at 6 seeds (0.675).
